statement: Use the state space, measure, and successor rule (7.1). Suppose the local kernel satisfies (7.3), and use the tail data and edge operator (7.5)–(7.6) with the bounds just proved. On L2 of states with these Bargmann fibers, give an allowed edge the operator-valued kernel eΦ(S′)−Φ(S) wθ(S, S′ ) µ(Y ) K(S, S′ ), (7.9) and give every other edge value zero. The choices of µ(Y ) used in this section are one, the indicator that every label is M or Fpair, and the products of the specified balanced periodized or infinite-volume B factors. Their per-particle factors have modulus at most one. For sufficiently large fixed b, these kernels are Hilbert–Schmidt uniformly in those choices and in θ ∈ D. The same conclusion permits fixed polynomial factors in the particle counts. For the fixed gauge on D, the kernels form holomorphic families in Hilbert–Schmidt norm on the open parameter neighborhood Uθ, with bounds uniform on compact subsets. 63 For a product of n ≥ 2 such kernels, its trace is the absolutely convergent integral over closed successor sequences, with the gauge factors canceled and the Bargmann trace given by (7.8). In particular, let Tj carry the specified periodized BT site factors for block j. Then, in increasing block order, tr n−1 Y j=0 Tj = det(I − An 0 )−1 Zm,bn. (7.10)
